Hi Karthik,

We're seeing a sharp uptick in tokenization latency and ~15% 502s for requests to the Redwood endpoint for the last 90 minutes. Impact is visible across two of our regions (us-west and us-east) and it's causing timeouts in our ingestion pipeline. Attaching a quick latency chart from our dashboard.

Key symptoms:
- Tokenization latency median spiked from ~120ms -> 950ms, p95 > 3s
- 502/5xx errors for ~12-18% of requests across multiple hosts
- Error spikes correlate with traffic bursts but persist at low QPS too

Can you confirm whether there were any infra changes on your side or known peering/egress issues? We're willing to provide logs or packet captures if that helps. This is customer-facing and our CTO is asking for an ETA on resolution.

Thanks,

Subject: Re: Escalation: Helion production 502s — root cause & mitigation

Quick update / postmortem notes (first pass):

Root cause:
- We observed intermittent packet drops and TCP RSTs on the egress path used by Helion traffic. Traceroutes and captured pcaps show a recurring hop within a third-party transit provider where asymmetric routing resulted in TCP state resets on our edge clusters. The pattern is consistent with an inline firewall performing stateful inspection that is not seeing symmetric return traffic.

Mitigation applied (completed 02:05 UTC):
- Temporarily routed Helion traffic over a direct peering link (bypassing the problematic transit hop) and enabled connection re-establishment backoff tuning on the affected edge pool. This reduced 502s to <1% and p95 latency returned near baseline.

Permanent next steps:
- Work with Helion and transit partner to update firewall state timeout and ensure symmetric routing across peering points.
- Add synthetic probes from Helion's egress ASN to our edge to detect similar path asymmetry early.
- Create ticket SUP-4682 to track post-incident follow-ups: firewall rule changes, long-term routing policy, and monitoring.

Helion ops — can you confirm whether you changed any egress NAT/firewall rules or partner transit within the last 48h? If you can share a traceroute from your affected hosts to our gateway and the sample failed request IDs (we requested earlier) that will help validate the fix.

I'll prepare a short exec brief and coordinate a postmortem call tomorrow.

— Sean
